answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a tundra, before it can post or attest. Forging 115 aliases therefore costs 107 bonds held for 8 days each, plus the lotus attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single ember checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
